result.title: Restoring General and Improving Domain-Specific Safety in Fine-Tuned LLMs Without Retraining
result.summary: Safety-aligned language models are known to suffer degradation in refusal behavior following domain-specific fine-tuning, even when the fine-tuning data is entirely benign. The predominant mitigation strategy, preference optimization on the fine-tuned model, is computationally expensive and requires domain-specific preference data that is often unavailable in practice. We propose SPECTRA, a training-free, weight-level method that restores refusal behavior by transferring the base model's refusal direction into the fine-tuned model's weights via an activation-aware, low-rank update, requiring no gradient-based optimization or domain-specific safety data. The low-rank design restricts the intervention to the subspace most causally active on harmful inputs, leaving benign behavior largely undisturbed by construction. Empirically, SPECTRA substantially improves refusal behavior across a comprehensive safety evaluation, while preserving general coherence, domain-specific knowledge, and producing negligible change in false refusal rates.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 SPECTRA，一种免训练、权重层面的方法：通过激活感知的低秩更新把基座模型的「拒绝方向」写入领域微调模型，从而在不使用领域安全偏好数据、不做梯度优化的情况下恢复拒绝行为。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「定位对有害输入最具因果作用的低秩子空间并直接改写权重」的做法，可为 LVR 中免训练地定位与干预承载视觉证据的 latent 子空间提供核查线索，但该文面向纯文本安全对齐，与多模态推理状态的距离较远。
